I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 26 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency declared on March 15, 1995 in Executive Order 12957, on which Executive Order 13553 states it relies. Notice of March 2, 2026 (91 FR 10937; FR Doc. 2026-04450) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond March 15, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only, naming EO 12957, EO 14382 of February 6, 2026 and the Notice of March 2, 2026, none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. Executive Order 14382 of February 6, 2026 recites this order as an example of additional steps and does not revoke or amend it (its text was searched for this number and for revocation language). Sections 5 through 8 delegate functions under CISADA sections 104 and 105 (22 U.S.C. 8513, 8514); the text of those statutory sections is not separately held, no held source repeals or limits them, and the claim treats the delegations as continuing because no held source ends them. Order 13553 of 2010-09-28 (75 FR 60567, PDF pages 1-5) is held as the Federal Register original (govinfo PDF text layer, grade official original). I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 26 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency declared on March 15, 1995 in Executive Order 12957, on which Executive Order 13553 states it relies. Notice of March 2, 2026 (91 FR 10937; FR Doc. 2026-04450) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond March 15, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only, naming EO 12957, EO 14382 of February 6, 2026 and the Notice of March 2, 2026, none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. Executive Order 14382 of February 6, 2026 recites this order as an example of additional steps and does not revoke or amend it (its text was searched for this number and for revocation language). Sections 5 through 8 delegate functions under CISADA sections 104 and 105 (22 U.S.C. 8513, 8514); the text of those statutory sections is not separately held, no held source repeals or limits them, and the claim treats the delegations as continuing because no held source ends them. I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 29 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency with respect to Libya declared in the lead clause of Executive Order 13566 on February 25, 2011 and expanded on April 19, 2016. Notice of February 13, 2026 (91 FR 7801; FR Doc. 2026-03279) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond February 25, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only, naming EO 13726 of April 19, 2016 and the Notice of February 13, 2026, none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause; Executive Order 13726 expands the emergency and is recorded on the lead clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. Executive Order 13726 of April 19, 2016 expanded the scope of the emergency and added its own blocking criteria; it does not amend the wording of this order and is recorded as a later event on the lead clause. I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 13 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13466 of June 26, 2008, and expanded in Executive Order 13551, on which Executive Order 13570 states it relies. Notice of June 22, 2026 (91 FR 38231; FR Doc. 2026-12836) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond June 26, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only, naming EO 13466, EO 13551, EO 13687 and annual continuation notices (June 13, 2022; June 20, 2025; June 22, 2026), none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. Later orders EO 13687 and EO 13810 recite this order or the emergency; they are recitals, not amendments or revocations. The import prohibition in section 1 is also reflected in OFAC regulations, which are not needed for the conclusion. Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency with respect to significant transnational criminal organizations declared in Executive Order 13581 of July 24, 2011, under which additional steps were taken in Executive Order 13863. Notice of July 13, 2026 (91 FR 44727; FR Doc. 2026-14454) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond July 24, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain EO 13863 of March 15, 2019 (listed as a later event on the clause it amended) and annual continuation notices (July 21, 2025 and July 13, 2026), none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. {"actor_id":"EO:13645","char_end":6373,"char_start":5325,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1773,"char_start":1096,"text":"(a) The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary \nof State, is hereby authorized to impose on a foreign financial institution \nthe sanctions described in subsection (b) of this section upon determining \nthat the foreign financial institution has, on or after the effective date of \nthis order: \n(i) knowingly conducted or facilitated any significant transaction related \nto the purchase or sale of Iranian rials or a derivative, swap, future, \nforward, or other similar contract whose value is based on the exchange \nrate of the Iranian rial; or \n(ii) maintained significant funds or accounts outside the territory of Iran \ndenominated in the Iranian rial."},{"char_end":2983,"char_start":2660,"text":"(c) The prohibitions in subsection (b) of this section apply except to \nthe extent provided by statutes, or in regulations, orders, directives, or \nlicenses that may be issued pursuant to this order, and notwithstanding \nany contract entered into or any license or permit granted prior to the \neffective date of this order."},{"char_end":5315,"char_start":4992,"text":"(c) The prohibitions in subsection (b) of this section apply except to \nthe extent provided by statutes, or in regulations, orders, directives, or \nlicenses that may be issued pursuant to this order, and notwithstanding \nany contract entered into or any license or permit granted prior to the \neffective date of this order."},{"char_end":6373,"char_start":5325,"text":"(a) The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary \nof State, is hereby authorized to impose on a foreign financial institution \nthe sanctions described in subsection (b) of this section upon determining \nthat the foreign financial institution has knowingly conducted or facilitated \nany significant financial transaction: \n(i) on behalf of any Iranian person included on the SDN List (other \nthan an Iranian depository institution whose property and interests in \nproperty are blocked solely pursuant to Executive Order 13599) or any \nother person included on the SDN List whose property and interests \nin property are blocked pursuant to subsection 2(a)(i) of this order or \nExecutive Order 13599 (other than an Iranian depository institution whose \nproperty and interests in property are blocked solely pursuant to Executive \nOrder 13599); or \n(ii) on or after the effective date of this order, for the sale, supply, or \ntransfer to Iran of significant goods or services used in connection with \nthe automotive sector of Iran."},{"char_end":9058,"char_start":8735,"text":"(f) The prohibitions in subsection (b) of this section apply except to \nthe extent provided by statutes, or in regulations, orders, directives, or \nlicenses that may be issued pursuant to this order, and notwithstanding \nany contract entered into or any license or permit granted prior to the \neffective date of this order."},{"char_end":10873,"char_start":9436,"text":"The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the \nTreasury, the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Homeland Security, \nand the United States Trade Representative, and with the President of the \nExport-Import Bank, the Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal \nReserve System, and other agencies and officials as appropriate, is hereby \nauthorized to impose on a person any of the sanctions described in section \n6 or 7 of this order upon determining that the person: \n(a) on or after the effective date of this order, knowingly engaged in \na significant transaction for the sale, supply, or transfer to Iran of significant \ngoods or services used in connection with the automotive sector of Iran; \n(b) is a successor entity to a person determined by the Secretary of State \nin accordance with this section to meet the criteria in subsection (a) of \nthis section; \n(c) owns or controls a person determined by the Secretary of State in \naccordance with this section to meet the criteria in subsection (a) of this \nsection, and had knowledge that the person engaged in the activities referred \nto in that subsection; or \n(d) is owned or controlled by, or under common ownership or control \nwith, a person determined by the Secretary of State in accordance with \nthis section to meet the criteria in subsection (a) of this section, and know-\ningly participated in the activities referred to in that subsection."},{"char_end":13888,"char_start":13560,"text":"(g) The prohibitions in subsections (a)–(f) of this section apply except \nto the extent provided by statutes, or in regulations, orders, directives, \nor licenses that may be issued pursuant to this order, and notwithstanding \nany contract entered into or any license or permit granted prior to the \neffective date of this order."},{"char_end":17188,"char_start":16865,"text":"(b) The prohibitions in subsection (a) of this section apply except to \nthe extent provided by statutes, or in regulations, orders, directives, or \nlicenses that may be issued pursuant to this order, and notwithstanding \nany contract entered into or any license or permit granted prior to the \neffective date of this order."},{"char_end":18994,"char_start":18671,"text":"(b) The prohibitions in subsection (a) of this section apply except to \nthe extent provided by statutes, or in regulations, orders, directives, or \nlicenses that may be issued pursuant to this order, and notwithstanding \nany contract entered into or any license or permit granted prior to the \neffective date of this order."},{"char_end":29273,"char_start":29016,"text":"I therefore determine that for these measures to be effective in addressing \nthe national emergency declared in Executive Order 12957, there need be \nno prior notice of an action taken pursuant to subsection 1(b)(ii), 2(b), \n7(a)(iv), or 8(a) of this order."},{"char_end":30310,"char_start":29862,"text":"(c) Subsection (a)(i) of section 2 is amended by replacing ‘‘knowingly, \non or after the effective date of this order, engaged in a significant transaction \nfor the purchase or acquisition of petroleum or petroleum products from \nIran’’ with ‘‘knowingly, on or after the effective date of this order, engaged \nin a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, \nor marketing of petroleum or petroleum products from Iran’’."},{"char_end":30744,"char_start":30312,"text":"(d) Subsection (a)(ii) of section 2 is amended by replacing ‘‘knowingly, \non or after the effective date of this order, engaged in a significant transaction \nfor the purchase or acquisition of petrochemical products from Iran’’ with \n‘‘knowingly, on or after the effective date of this order, engaged in a signifi-\ncant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing \nof petrochemical products from Iran’’."},{"char_end":31963,"char_start":31886,"text":"This order is effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July \n1, 2013."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:13599>EO:13645@36e8f7bc19fc9f7b","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 3.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["It includes but is not limited to depository institutions, \nbanks, savings banks, money service businesses, trust companies, securities \nbrokers and dealers, commodity futures and options brokers and dealers, \nforward contract and foreign exchange merchants, securities and commodities \nexchanges, clearing corporations, investment companies, employee benefit \nplans, dealers in precious metals, stones, or jewels, and holding companies, \naffiliates, or subsidiaries of any of the foregoing.","The term does not include \nthe international financial institutions identified in 22 U.S.C. 262r(c)(2), \nthe International Fund for Agricultural Development, the North American \nDevelopment Bank, or any other international financial institution so notified \nby the Secretary of the Treasury; \n(e) the term ‘‘Government of Iran’’ includes the Government of Iran, any \npolitical subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including the Central \nVerDate Mar<15>2010 19:51 Jun 04, 2013 Jkt 226001 PO 00000 Frm 00006 Fmt 4790 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\05JNE0.SGM 05JNE0mstockstill on DSK4VPTVN1PROD with PREDOCE0\n=== PDF page 7 of 9 ===\n33951 Federal Register / Vol. 78, No. 108 / Wednesday, June 5, 2013 / Presidential Documents \nBank of Iran, and any person owned or controlled by, or acting for or \non behalf of, the Government of Iran; \n(f) the term ‘‘Iran’’ means the Government of Iran and the territory of \nIran and any other territory or marine area, including the exclusive economic \nzone and continental shelf, over which the Government of Iran claims sov-\nereignty, sovereign rights, or jurisdiction, provided that the Government \nof Iran exercises partial or total de facto control over the area or derives \na benefit from economic activity in the area pursuant to international arrange-\nments; \n(g) the term ‘‘Iranian depository institution’’ means any entity (including \nforeign branches), wherever located, organized under the laws of Iran or \nany jurisdiction within Iran, or owned or controlled by the Government \nof Iran, or in Iran, or owned or controlled by any of the foregoing, that \nis engaged primarily in the business of banking (for example, banks, savings \nbanks, savings associations, credit unions, trust companies, and bank holding \ncompanies); \n(h) the term ‘‘Iranian person,’’ as used in sections 2 and 3 of this order, \nmeans an individual who is a citizen or national of Iran or an entity \norganized under the laws of Iran or otherwise subject to the jurisdiction \nof the Government of Iran; \n(i) the terms ‘‘knowledge’’ and ‘‘knowingly,’’ with respect to conduct, \na circumstance, or a result, mean that a person has actual knowledge, or \nshould have known, of the conduct, the circumstance, or the result; \n(j) the term ‘‘person’’ means an individual or entity; \n(k) the term ‘‘petroleum’’ (also known as crude oil) means a mixture \nof hydrocarbons that exists in liquid phase in natural underground reservoirs \nand remains liquid at atmospheric pressure after passing through surface \nseparating facilities; \n(l) the term ‘‘petroleum products’’ includes unfinished oils, liquefied petro-\nleum gases, pentanes plus, aviation gasoline, motor gasoline, naphtha-type \njet fuel, kerosene-type jet fuel, kerosene, distillate fuel oil, residual fuel \noil, petrochemical feedstocks, special naphthas, lubricants, waxes, petroleum \ncoke, asphalt, road oil, still gas, and miscellaneous products obtained from \nthe processing of: crude oil (including lease condensate), natural gas, and \nother hydrocarbon compounds."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2013-06-03","target_id":"EO:13599","verb":"transfer"}

\n(f) the term ‘‘Iran’’ means the Government of Iran and the territory of \nIran and any other territory or marine area, including the exclusive economic \nzone and continental shelf, over which the Government of Iran claims sov-\nereignty, sovereign rights, or jurisdiction, provided that the Government \nof Iran exercises partial or total de facto control over the area or derives \na benefit from economic activity in the area pursuant to international arrange-\nments; \n(g) the term ‘‘Iranian depository institution’’ means any entity (including \nforeign branches), wherever located, organized under the laws of Iran or \nany jurisdiction within Iran, or owned or controlled by the Government \nof Iran, or in Iran, or owned or controlled by any of the foregoing, that \nis engaged primarily in the business of banking (for example, banks, savings \nbanks, savings associations, credit unions, trust companies, and bank holding \ncompanies); \n(h) the term ‘‘Iranian person,’’ as used in sections 2 and 3 of this order, \nmeans an individual who is a citizen or national of Iran or an entity \norganized under the laws of Iran or otherwise subject to the jurisdiction \nof the Government of Iran; \n(i) the terms ‘‘knowledge’’ and ‘‘knowingly,’’ with respect to conduct, \na circumstance, or a result, mean that a person has actual knowledge, or \nshould have known, of the conduct, the circumstance, or the result; \n(j) the term ‘‘person’’ means an individual or entity; \n(k) the term ‘‘petroleum’’ (also known as crude oil) means a mixture \nof hydrocarbons that exists in liquid phase in natural underground reservoirs \nand remains liquid at atmospheric pressure after passing through surface \nseparating facilities; \n(l) the term ‘‘petroleum products’’ includes unfinished oils, liquefied petro-\nleum gases, pentanes plus, aviation gasoline, motor gasoline, naphtha-type \njet fuel, kerosene-type jet fuel, kerosene, distillate fuel oil, residual fuel \noil, petrochemical feedstocks, special naphthas, lubricants, waxes, petroleum \ncoke, asphalt, road oil, still gas, and miscellaneous products obtained from \nthe processing of: crude oil (including lease condensate), natural gas, and \nother hydrocarbon compounds."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2013-06-03","target_id":"EO:13599","verb":"transfer"}

\n(n) the term ‘‘petroleum’’ (also known as crude oil) means a mixture \nof hydrocarbons that exists in liquid phase in natural underground reservoirs \nand remains liquid at atmospheric pressure after passing through surface \nseparating facilities; \n(o) the term ‘‘petroleum products’’ includes unfinished oils, liquefied petro-\nleum gases, pentanes plus, aviation gasoline, motor gasoline, naphtha-type \njet fuel, kerosene-type jet fuel, kerosene, distillate fuel oil, residual fuel \noil, petrochemical feedstocks, special naphthas, lubricants, waxes, petroleum \ncoke, asphalt, road oil, still gas, and miscellaneous products obtained from \nthe processing of: crude oil (including lease condensate), natural gas, and \nother hydrocarbon compounds.","(a) Pursuant to section 202 of the NEA \n(50 U.S.C. 1622), the revocation of Executive Orders 13716 and 13628 as \nset forth in section 9 of this order, shall not affect any action taken or \nproceeding pending not finally concluded or determined as of the effective \ndate of this order, or any action or proceeding based on any act committed \nprior to the effective date of this order, or any rights or duties that matured \nor penalties that were incurred prior to the effective date of this order."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2018-08-06","target_id":"EO:13599","verb":"transfer"}

Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 2.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["It includes, but is not limited \nto, depository institutions, banks, savings banks, money service businesses, \ntrust companies, securities brokers and dealers, commodity futures and op-\ntions brokers and dealers, forward contract and foreign exchange merchants, \nsecurities and commodities exchanges, clearing corporations, investment \ncompanies, employee benefit plans, dealers in precious metals, stones, or \njewels, and holding companies, affiliates, or subsidiaries of any of the fore-\ngoing.","The term does not include the international financial institutions \nidentified in 22 U.S.C. 262r(c)(2), the International Fund for Agricultural \nDevelopment, the North American Development Bank, or any other inter-\nnational financial institution so notified by the Secretary of the Treasury; \n(e) the term ‘‘Government of Iran’’ includes the Government of Iran, any \npolitical subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including the Central \nBank of Iran, and any person owned or controlled by, or acting for or \non behalf of, the Government of Iran; \n(f) the term ‘‘Iran’’ means the Government of Iran and the territory of \nIran and any other territory or marine area, including the exclusive economic \nzone and continental shelf, over which the Government of Iran claims sov-\nereignty, sovereign rights, or jurisdiction, provided that the Government \nof Iran exercises partial or total de facto control over the area or derives \na benefit from economic activity in the area pursuant to international arrange-\nments; \n(g) the term ‘‘Iranian depository institution’’ means any entity (including \nforeign branches), wherever located, organized under the laws of Iran or \nany jurisdiction within Iran, or owned or controlled by the Government \nof Iran, or in Iran, or owned or controlled by any of the foregoing, that \nis engaged primarily in the business of banking (for example, banks, savings \nbanks, savings associations, credit unions, trust companies, and bank holding \ncompanies); \n(h) the term ‘‘Iranian person’’ means an individual who is a citizen or \nnational of Iran or an entity organized under the laws of Iran or otherwise \nsubject to the jurisdiction of the Government of Iran; \n(i) the terms ‘‘knowledge’’ and ‘‘knowingly,’’ with respect to conduct, \na circumstance, or a result, mean that a person has actual knowledge, or \nshould have known, of the conduct, the circumstance, or the result; \n(j) the terms ‘‘Naftiran Intertrade Company’’ and ‘‘NICO’’ mean the Naftiran \nIntertrade Company Ltd. and any entity owned or controlled by, or operating \nfor or on behalf of, the Naftiran Intertrade Company Ltd.; \n(k) the terms ‘‘National Iranian Oil Company’’ and ‘‘NIOC’’ mean the \nNational Iranian Oil Company and any entity owned or controlled by, or \noperating for or on behalf of, the National Iranian Oil Company; \n(n) the term ‘‘petroleum’’ (also known as crude oil) means a mixture \nof hydrocarbons that exists in liquid phase in natural underground reservoirs \nand remains liquid at atmospheric pressure after passing through surface \nseparating facilities; \n(o) the term ‘‘petroleum products’’ includes unfinished oils, liquefied petro-\nleum gases, pentanes plus, aviation gasoline, motor gasoline, naphtha-type \njet fuel, kerosene-type jet fuel, kerosene, distillate fuel oil, residual fuel \noil, petrochemical feedstocks, special naphthas, lubricants, waxes, petroleum \ncoke, asphalt, road oil, still gas, and miscellaneous products obtained from \nthe processing of: crude oil (including lease condensate), natural gas, and \nother hydrocarbon compounds.","(a) Pursuant to section 202 of the NEA \n(50 U.S.C. 1622), the revocation of Executive Orders 13716 and 13628 as \nset forth in section 9 of this order, shall not affect any action taken or \nproceeding pending not finally concluded or determined as of the effective \ndate of this order, or any action or proceeding based on any act committed \nprior to the effective date of this order, or any rights or duties that matured \nor penalties that were incurred prior to the effective date of this order."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2018-08-06","target_id":"EO:13599","verb":"transfer"}

I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 24 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency declared on March 15, 1995 in Executive Order 12957, on which Executive Order 13599 states it relies. Notice of March 2, 2026 (91 FR 10937; FR Doc. 2026-04450) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond March 15, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only, naming EO 12170, EO 12281, EO 12957, EO 13628 and the Notice of March 2, 2026, none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. EO 13645 of June 3, 2013 and EO 13846 of August 6, 2018 refer to property blocked solely pursuant to this order; they presuppose it and neither amends nor revokes it. Sections 10 and 11 delegate functions under section 1245(d) of the NDAA; the current text of that statutory section is not separately held, no held source repeals or limits it, and the claim treats the delegations as continuing because no held source ends them. I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 26 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency declared on March 15, 1995 in Executive Order 12957, on which Executive Order 13606 relies as to Iran. Notice of March 2, 2026 (91 FR 10937; FR Doc. 2026-04450) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond March 15, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain EO 14312 of June 30, 2025 (listed as a later event on the lead clause, whose preamble it amended), plus cross-references to EO 12957, EO 13338 and the Notice of March 2, 2026. The only later textual change found is Executive Order 14312 section 4(b), which rewrote the preamble; it is recorded as a later event on the lead clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. Executive Order 14312 section 4(b) rewrote the preamble reference to the Syria emergency (Executive Order 13338) as a reference to Executive Order 13894 and did not revoke this order, which Executive Order 14312 amends rather than revokes. Executive Order 14312 is held as an American Presidency Project mirror transcription (grade mirror_transcription); its working-text confirmation is recorded in working_text, original not yet held; replace and re-check when an official copy is registered for this packet. I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 22 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency with respect to Yemen declared in the lead clause of Executive Order 13611 on May 16, 2012. Notice of May 7, 2026 (Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 90, May 11, 2026; FR Doc. 2026-09385) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond May 16, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only: the Notice of May 9, 2022 and an entry labelled Proc. 11026, May 5, 2026, discussed below. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. The Federal Register index of order notes labels a cross-reference to Proc. 11026 of May 5, 2026; its text is not held in the repository and the entry is a See reference, not a revoked-by or superseded-by note. The Notice of May 7, 2026, issued two days later, states that the Yemen emergency declared in this order must continue in effect beyond May 16, 2026, which is inconsistent with any ending of the order by that proclamation.
